appliesToWhy: GA appendix B curl list (13) minus wrist_curl, which is exempt (wrist-curl-exemption.json).

thumbRule.text: Closed grip, thumbs wrapped round the handle.

wrist.text: Straight, in line with the forearm, neither bent up nor down, for the whole lift.

rightPose.text: Closed grip, thumb wrapped, wrist straight in line with the forearm while the elbow bends.

faults.label: Wrist curled
faults.what: Wrist bent forward (flexed) during the curl.

widthNote.text: If holding the dumbbells at your sides bends your wrists, hold them where your wrists stay straight.

gripLine.text: Wrap your thumbs round the handle and keep your wrists straight, in line with your forearms.

claims.text: For dumbbell curls, take a closed grip with the thumbs wrapped round the handles.

quotes.text: Grasp two dumbbells with a closed, supinated grip (palms facing forward and thumbs wrapped around the handles)

claims.text: The hammer curl uses the same closed grip with the thumbs round the handles, palms facing the body.

quotes.text: Stand holding dumbbells in your hands with a closed, neutral grip (thumbs around the handles with your palms facing your body).

claims.text: Keep the wrist neutral through the curl: avoid bending it forward (flexion) or back (extension).

quotes.text: Maintain a neutral wrist position (avoid flexion and extension of your wrists)
Maintain a neutral wrist position (wrist straight without any bend with your palms facing your body)

claims.text: Keep the wrists straight during the curl; bent wrists put unnecessary load on them and can lead to discomfort or injury.

quotes.text: Not locking your wrists. Keep your wrists straight during the movement. If they’re bent, it can put an unnecessary load on them and lead to discomfort and maybe even injuries.

claims.text: Because elbow structure differs, some people cannot hold the dumbbells against their sides at the bottom without bending the wrist; choose the dumbbell position that keeps the wrist straight with the forearm.

quotes.text: As some of us show structural differences at the elbow, we may not be able to hold the dumbbells against our sides in the lowered position unless we force a bend at our wrists.
The dumbbell position selected should be one that is most comfortable for you and keeps the wrists aligned straight with the forearm.

sources.title: How to Dumbbell Curl: Muscles Worked & Proper Form (StrengthLog)

gaps: Contact point: no source read says where the handle sits in the palm (GA: across the middle of the palm). Drawn as GA's default, recorded as a drawing convention, not a claim.

The thumb and wrist rules are sourced on dumbbell curls (seated curl, hammer curl, standing curl). They are applied to barbell, EZ-bar, cable and preacher curls by inference; their own verified cards carry their own wrist claims (barbell_curl c8, ez_bar_curl c8, preacher_curl c8, reverse_curl c6, cable_curl c9).

The fault names wrist-curl-cheat and bent-back-bottom come from GA; the sources name the wrong positions (flexion, extension, a forced bend at the bottom), not a cheating motion. The labels describe positions only.
notes: Same rules sourced in cards/dumbbell_biceps_curl.json c1, c6, c7 and cards/hammer_curl.json c1, c4, c10 (ACE, StrengthLog). Re-read ACE seated curl, ACE hammer curl and StrengthLog dumbbell curl in full on 2026-10-01; quotes copied from that read.
Reverse curls are overhand, hammer curls neutral and the rest underhand; orientation is a per-exercise drawing parameter (GA 3.3), not part of this rule.
